verdict: Lilly's revenue rose 20% to $11.4B as Mounjaro more than doubled to $3.1B and Zepbound added $1.3B — but a $2.8B charge for research bought in the Morphic acquisition held reported profit to $970M.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — revenue more than doubled on strong demand and increased supply, despite U.S. wholesaler inventory drawdowns late in the quarter.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot (tirzepatide), launched in the U.S. in November 2023 — already $1.3B a quarter.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — Verzenio, Taltz, Jardiance, Humalog and the older brands. Down on paper only: a year ago included $1.42B from selling the rights to the olanzapine portfolio (Zyprexa).

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and the back office — up 16% on launch spending.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought with acquisitions, charged at once — mostly the Morphic Holding deal.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Mostly an impairment on an intangible asset tied to a molecule in development.

otherDetail: Net other income of $62M — $207M of net other income, partly offset by $145M of net interest expense.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $1,065M (EPS $1.18). The release reports figures to one decimal place; they are rounded to whole millions here.

takeaways.title: Growth, adjusting for a divestiture
takeaways.text: Reported revenue rose 20% — but the year-ago quarter included $1.42B from selling the rights to the olanzapine portfolio (Zyprexa). Excluding that one-off, revenue grew 42%, and revenue from everything except the weight-loss and diabetes shots grew 17%.

takeaways.title: Two shots are 38% of revenue
takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($3.11B, +121%) and Zepbound ($1.26B, launched November 2023) together brought in $4.4B of the $11.4B total. U.S. sales of both were trimmed a mid-single-digit percent by wholesalers running down inventories built up in Q2.

takeaways.title: The Morphic charge
takeaways.text: Lilly booked a $2,826M acquired IPR&D charge, mostly for buying Morphic Holding, plus an $82M impairment. The charge is largely not tax-deductible, which pushed the reported tax rate to 38.9% — and reported profit to $970M (EPS $1.07), versus a $57M loss a year ago.

oneTimers: Acquired in-process R&D of $2,826M — mostly the Morphic Holding acquisition, which closed in August 2024 — plus $82M of asset impairment and restructuring charges. Lilly's non-GAAP net income of $1,065M (EPS $1.18) excludes the impairment-type charges; Lilly still counts IPR&D in its non-GAAP figures.
The year-ago quarter's revenue included $1,420M from the sale of rights for the olanzapine portfolio (Zyprexa) — a one-off that makes the reported +20% growth look slower than the underlying +42%.

Guidance moved down with this release: Lilly set 2024 revenue guidance at $45.4–$46.0B and reported EPS at $12.05–$12.55, after wholesaler inventory drawdowns trimmed Mounjaro and Zepbound sales in the quarter.
